name: Cyclotomic supplementarity
summary: n Z-states whose phases α + 2kπ/n divide the circle into equal parts, attached to one X-spider, merge into one Z-spider with phase nα+(n−1)π connected by n wires.
description:
A generalisation of [supplementarity](../supplementarity/) from two to $n$ dots: if $n$ arity-one Z-spiders with phases $\alpha, \alpha+\frac{2\pi}n, \ldots, \alpha+\frac{(n-1)2\pi}n$ are attached to the same X-spider, they can be merged into a single Z-spider with phase $n\alpha+(n-1)\pi$, connected to the X-spider by $n$ parallel wires. Supplementarity is the case $n=2$.

Jeandel, Perdrix, Vilmart and Wang showed that $(\mathrm{SUP}_n)$ cannot be derived from the other rules when $n$ is an odd prime, giving a countable family of necessary axioms, while for composite $n$ it follows from the rules for its factors. As for supplementarity, the dots can more generally be merged when they have the same neighbourhood (*cyclotomic twins*).
parameter_notes: Shown for n = 3, where the merged phase 3α + 2π equals 3α. The rule holds for every n ≥ 1, with the phases depending on n.
